text.title: Retainer Pricing Methodology — Decision Tree
text.summary: Routing tree mapping observable engagement signals (recurring scope, shape chosen, price against hourly-equivalent, capacity) to a rule from `01-core-rules.xml`. Every leaf references a rule id.

decision-tree.root-question: Does the client have recurring work in the same scope for at least 3 months ahead (maintenance, ongoing feature stream, on-call availability), rather than a single bounded project?

conclusion.verdict: no capacity to retain; price it as a fixed-scope project and revisit when a second engagement appears

branch.question: Does the draft name exactly one retainer shape (block-of-hours, outcome-based, availability) with its defining term (rollover and overage, deliverable list, or response time and maximum load)?

conclusion.verdict: pick the shape from the client's actual request pattern before pricing anything

branch.question: Is the monthly price shown as expected hours x hourly rate x multiple, with the multiple at or above 1.3 (or a named client concession justifying less)?

conclusion.verdict: re-price with the three numbers visible; if the client refuses the floor, shrink the block rather than the rate

branch.question: Do total committed hours across all active retainers, including this one at maximum load, stay within available billable hours?

conclusion.verdict: do not sign; end or re-scope another retainer first, or reduce this one's maximum load
write the artefact with scope lists, turnaround, term and notice, advance billing, cutover date if converting from hourly, and the 6-month review

text.example: recurring_scope=true -> shape_named=true -> price_above_floor=true -> capacity_fits=true -> conclusion ref=run-the-checklist
